name: Shay Pruitt
equipment: Ruger .22 pistol with a threaded suppressor (10-round magazine), 'found' in a house in Haskett
A box of .22 shells she pocketed in Kettering's (included in the count above)
A cheap phone with a cracked screen and one contact saved as 'W'
features: Specialist (Human (Specialist): +2 Dexterity, +1 Charisma, extra skill proficiency in Perception)
Expertise (double proficiency bonus in Stealth and Sleight of Hand: +7 each)
Precision Strike (once per turn, +1d6 damage with a finesse melee or sidearm/longarm attack when she has advantage or an ally is within 5 ft of the target)
Criminal Contact (Criminal feature: she knows every fence, dealer and back-door operator in the county, and which of them are still alive)

personality.traits: I make a joke about everything, especially things that scare me. I know where the exits are in every room. I steal small things without noticing I am doing it.
personality.ideals: Look after yourself, because nobody else is going to. (I would like very much to be wrong about this.)
personality.bonds: My brother Wade. He raised me after Mom left, and then he became a cop, and then he arrested me, twice. I love him and I cannot be in a room with him.
personality.flaws: When it gets bad I run. I always have. I have been running from Wade since I was nineteen.

appearance: Twenty-four, small and quick, with choppy dyed-black hair, a silver lip ring, chipped black nail polish and an oversized leather jacket with the sleeves pushed up. Has very fast hands and a habit of standing with her back to walls. Looks younger than she is until she smiles, and then looks older.
backstory: Shay Pruitt grew up in a trailer on the Haskett road with her older brother Wade, who raised her more or less single-handed after their mother left, and then joined the sheriff's department and spent six years trying to keep her out of trouble — which included arresting her twice for burglary. She has stolen car stereos, prescription pills and, once, a riding mower. On the Saturday of Ferry Days she was in Kettering Hardware & Feed pocketing a box of .22 shells for the pistol she had taken from a house in Haskett the week before when old Arlo Kettering caught her, looked at her for a long time, and said, 'Well, sit down then.' She was still sitting on the feed sacks deciding whether to run when the screaming started.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Shay is the party's Operative companion and the campaign's personal line into the Co-op. Introduce her in Kettering's in ob-scenario-001. She is funny, quick, useful (her suppressed .22 is the only quiet gun in the party for a long time — make sure the players notice it) and unreliable in exactly the ways she warns them about. She will steal from the party's supplies once, in a small way, early on, and then — if they handle it decently — never again. Her arc is about stopping running: from the dead, from the party, and finally from her brother.
dmNotes.voice: Fast, sarcastic, rural-Missouri vowels she tries to hide, a lot of 'babe' and 'dude', and long silences when anyone mentions family. When she is genuinely frightened she gets very quiet and very polite. Swears creatively but never in front of Maddie.
dmNotes.motivations: Survive. Not be caught. And, though she will not say it, find out whether Wade is alive — and then avoid him.
dmNotes.secrets: From ob-scenario-002 onward, after the party crosses the Co-op census, Shay is passing small pieces of news about the party to Wade on the Co-op's radio channel (via the cheap phone's walkie app while the towers last, then a Co-op handheld she steals): where they are, how many, that they are good people. She is doing it so Wade will keep the Co-op away from them, and she believes it is working. It is — until ob-scenario-003, when Colleen Marsh reads Wade's notes and puts Kettering's in her ledger as 'A-list: 2. Monitor.' If the party discovers this, Shay will confess at once and completely, and her worst fear is that they will throw her out. In ob-scenario-003 she is the person most able to make Wade surrender the Bell.
dmNotes.attitude: To the party: suspicious, then attached, then fiercely loyal, and frightened of how loyal. To Maddie: a big sister, instantly and without discussion. To Arlo: she was going to rob him and he gave her a seat, and she does not have words for that. To Wade: love, rage and terror in about equal parts. To the Co-op: 'It's just cops with corn.'
